grammar_features.description: 15 reusable call operators. Quantifiers range over the specified finite observation collections. Temporal operators use the current invocation trace: always means every state from the current state onward; previously means some earlier state; eventually means some current or future state; next_state means the next state. Explicit event interval comparisons must restrict lifetime-specific obligations. Mathematical integers are used for arithmetic, including pointer offsets, without implicit machine wrapping.

types.name: Value
types.description: A typed value of any type.

fields.name: address
fields.description: The numeric address of the value.

fields.name: value
fields.description: The actual value, which may be a primitive or a structured object.

fields.name: type
fields.description: The actual source type of this value.

fields.name: call
fields.description: Invocation in which this value is bound, available also on pointers and unit results.

fields.name: length
fields.description: Array/slice/string length; elements for arrays/slices, bytes for strings.

fields.name: element_type
fields.description: Array/slice/pointer pointee element type.

fields.name: elements
fields.description: The source elements, in index order, each carrying source index and type.

fields.name: bytes
fields.description: Object-representation bytes, each with numeric value and initialization state; padding may be uninitialized.

fields.name: variant
fields.description: Active enum variant, e.g. Some, None, Ok or Err.

fields.name: index
fields.description: Index of an element within its parent sequence.

fields.name: initialized
fields.description: The source value has been initialized according to Rust value initialization, not all padding bytes.

fields.name: discriminant
fields.description: Numeric enum discriminant.

fields.name: is_nan
fields.description: IEEE floating-point NaN classification.

fields.name: is_infinite
fields.description: IEEE floating-point infinity classification.

fields.name: truncated
fields.description: The mathematical integer obtained by truncation toward zero, for finite floating-point values.

fields.name: observations
fields.description: All source invocations on this object, including arguments, results, pre/post-state and event interval.

fields.name: identity
fields.description: Stable source object identity, preserved through references.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: Creation event position in the program trace.

fields.name: dropped_at
fields.description: Drop completion event position, or None if not dropped.

fields.name: region
fields.description: Address-space region such as user or enclave, derived from the platform memory map.

fields.name: lifetime
fields.description: Source borrow or future lifetime interval, with start/end trace positions.

fields.name: descendants
fields.description: The transitive reflexive closure of real source fields/elements of this value; pointer pointees are not followed unless the source owns that pointee.

fields.name: reachable
fields.description: Transitive reflexive closure of the actual source pointer/reference/field graph, with cycle deduplication; this is graph reachability, not a validity flag.

fields.name: states
fields.description: The same source value/object viewed at each trace position. Pointer identity/address are retained; pointee, allocation, permissions and resource state reflect the selected position, including after deallocation.

fields.name: resource
fields.description: The modeled OS/platform resource denoted by a descriptor, handle, socket, task identifier or user allocation; None for invalid/non-resource values.

types.name: Pointer
types.description: Rust raw pointer, reference, or NonNull-like pointer value.

fields.name: address
fields.description: The numeric address.

fields.name: allocation
fields.description: The allocation/provenance object the pointer is derived from.

fields.name: offset
fields.description: The byte offset from the start of its allocation.

fields.name: is_null
fields.description: Whether the pointer address is zero.

fields.name: length
fields.description: Slice fat-pointer metadata length in elements.

fields.name: element_type
fields.description: Actual source pointee/element type.

fields.name: pointee
fields.description: The pointed-to source value, with its source fields; meaningful when dereferenceable.

fields.name: metadata
fields.description: DST pointer metadata: length scalar for slices or vtable pointer for trait objects.

fields.name: nul_offset
fields.description: Distance in bytes to first initialized NUL, or None if no reachable initialized NUL exists.

fields.name: wide_nul_offset
fields.description: Distance in 16-bit units to first initialized zero unit, or None.

fields.name: dynamic_size
fields.description: Entire source pointee size including static prefix and dynamic tail.

fields.name: dynamic_align
fields.description: Alignment of the actual dynamic pointee type.

fields.name: derived_from
fields.description: Transitive provenance/borrow ancestors, not address coincidence.

types.name: Allocation
types.description: Abstract allocation object maintained by the verifier.

fields.name: start
fields.description: The allocation start address.

fields.name: size
fields.description: The allocation size in bytes.

fields.name: written
fields.description: Whether every byte in the allocation has been written according to KLEE's source-level initialization mask.

fields.name: end
fields.description: The first address after the allocation.

fields.name: layout
fields.description: The original layout associated with this allocation.

fields.name: allocator
fields.description: The allocator identity that created this allocation.

fields.name: live
fields.description: Allocation exists and has not yet been deallocated at the evaluated state.

fields.name: minimum_size
fields.description: Minimum allocated size accepted by the allocator fitting-layout contract.

fields.name: region
fields.description: Platform address-space region, e.g. user or enclave.

types.name: MemoryRange
types.description: A half-open byte range [start, end) derived from a pointer and a size.

fields.name: start
fields.description: The first address in the range.

fields.name: size
fields.description: The range size in bytes.

fields.name: end
fields.description: The first address after the range.

fields.name: allocation
fields.description: The allocation containing the range start.

fields.name: region
fields.description: user or enclave iff the entire numerical address interval lies in that platform address-space region; mixed otherwise. Region membership does not imply allocation containment, initialization or access permission.

fields.name: size
fields.description: The layout size.

fields.name: align
fields.description: The layout alignment.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Stable verifier-local allocator id.

types.name: TypeInfo
types.description: Verifier view of a type argument at the target callsite.

fields.name: size
fields.description: size_of::<T>() when known, otherwise a symbolic value.

fields.name: align
fields.description: align_of::<T>() when known, otherwise a symbolic value.

fields.name: is_zst
fields.description: Whether the pointee type is zero-sized.

fields.name: allows_uninitialized
fields.description: Whether a value of this Rust type may legally be wholly uninitialized. KLEE derives this from concrete callsite type metadata (including MaybeUninit); unresolved external types remain explicit symbolic type inputs and inherit the callsite's certainty classification.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Canonical Rust source type name.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Rust nominal type identity, used for Any downcasts.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: Type category: primitive, struct, enum, array, slice, trait_object, extern, reference, raw_pointer, etc.

fields.name: sized
fields.description: Whether the source type implements Sized.

fields.name: tail_kind
fields.description: DST tail category: sized, slice, trait_object, extern or other.

fields.name: min
fields.description: Minimum representable integer value, for an integer type.

fields.name: max
fields.description: Maximum representable integer value, for an integer type.

fields.name: traits
fields.description: Implemented Rust traits, including marker/auto traits, from source type checking.

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Actual source field types, including nested source structure via recursive projections.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The transitive reflexive closure of source field/element types, with cycle deduplication; reference/raw-pointer targets are not ownership components.

fields.name: item_name
fields.description: Unqualified source type-item identifier, without module path or generic arguments.

fields.name: item_path
fields.description: Fully qualified defining Rust item path without generic arguments, e.g. std::os::fortanix_sgx::usercalls::alloc::User; distinct from an unrelated type with the same item_name.

fields.name: pointee_type
fields.description: Source pointee type of a raw pointer/reference or transparent pointer wrapper.

fields.name: tail_type
fields.description: Actual unsized tail type, or this type if the entire type is the tail.

fields.name: lang_item
fields.description: The actual Rust compiler lang-item identity, such as owned_box for Box; None for ordinary types.

fields.name: ownership
fields.description: owning for a source type whose contract owns pointee resources (Box, Vec, Rc, Arc and equivalent owner types); borrowed for references; raw for non-owning raw pointers; none otherwise. Ownership is distinct from mere pointer layout or reference access permissions.

fields.name: outlives
fields.description: Source lifetime bounds satisfied by this type, including static exactly when the type contains no non-static borrowed data under Rust outlives checking.

fields.name: associated_types
fields.description: Resolved source associated types, keyed by source name.

fields.name: has_padding
fields.description: Whether the Rust layout contains any padding bytes.

fields.name: has_provenance
fields.description: Whether the type can carry pointer provenance.

fields.name: bit_patterns
fields.description: All bit patterns of the type size, interpreted as candidate values.

fields.name: valid_bit_patterns
fields.description: Those patterns satisfying Rust language-level validity, independent of type safety invariants.

fields.name: valid_values
fields.description: All values obeying this source type and its safety invariants; distinct from merely language-bit-valid representations.

fields.name: subtypes
fields.description: Rust subtypes, as determined by source typing and variance.

fields.name: supertypes
fields.description: Rust supertypes, as determined by source typing and variance.

fields.name: implementations
fields.description: Source trait implementations with type, trait, method and associated-constant maps.

types.name: CallContext
types.description: Source invocation context. consts maps actual const generic names to values (including structured const parameters); constants maps source in-scope constants by name. args is the ordered source-argument sequence; result is the source result; receiver is arg0 for methods; result_type is TypeInfo; name is the source method name. start/end are trace event positions; thread is caller thread identity. before/after are State snapshots; events is the complete source execution trace (explicit intervals restrict scope). invocations is the collection of source invocations relevant to a trait contract. globals is the actual source global-variable map; platform is the target OS name; threads is the set of program threads. lifetimes maps source lifetime names to intervals with start/end. status is return, panic, unwind or abort; a future result has its lifetime interval via lifetime. source declarations and method names are not treated as precomputed rule-correctness predicates.

types.name: Invocation
types.description: A call observation with name (unqualified source method), qualified_name, args, receiver, result, result_type, before, after, start, end, thread, status; same meaning as CallContext. Snapshots expose real source fields and global maps. Events/invocations can include hypothetical permitted inputs when universally quantifying a trait implementation contract.

types.name: Event
types.description: A source execution event. kind is read, write, move, drop, deallocate, clone, borrow_shared, borrow_mut, call, return, panic, unwind, atomic, fence or undefined_behavior; time is its trace position; thread is its thread identity; object is the affected Value/ObjectId; range is the affected MemoryRange; pointer is the access pointer; value is the written or returned value; method is the source callee name for calls; args is source arguments; receiver is the receiver; result is the return value; ordering is the source atomic ordering; happens_before is the set of event identities ordered before this event; identity is the event identity; atomic is whether the access is atomic; unsafe_cell is whether the accessed bytes are inside UnsafeCell; derived_from is the set of source reference/object provenance ancestors of the access; lifetime is a borrow interval (start/end); instruction is the target instruction mnemonic for platform barriers.

types.name: State
types.description: A trace snapshot. globals is a map of actual source globals; objects is the set of source objects with their real fields and identities; allocations is the allocation set; threads is the thread set. Field access on a recorded receiver denotes its source state at that observation, rather than a fresh independent Boolean variable.

types.name: VTable
types.description: Compiler trait-object metadata: type is the actual concrete TypeInfo for which the vtable was emitted; target is the coercion target trait-object TypeInfo; trait is the implemented trait identity; origin is unsizing when this metadata was obtained by a Rust unsizing coercion; methods is the actual compiler-emitted method map. An initialized pointer to an unrelated vtable does not establish that it is the required type/trait vtable.

types.name: Resource
types.description: OS/platform resource state, independent of Rust owner-object existence. identity is its stable resource identity; kind is file_descriptor, socket, handle, task, event, module, process_environment or user_allocation. open is current liveness (includes inherited and foreign-created resources). owners is the set of logical ownership principals/tokens, independent of whether an OwnedFd/OwnedHandle value currently exists. closer is the operation sufficient to release it: close, closesocket, CloseHandle, RegCloseKey, SOLID_NET_Close (Rust source alias close) or the relevant free usercall, as determined by the platform resource class. created_at and closed_at are lifecycle event positions (closed_at None when open); attributes is the actual platform resource attribute map, e.g. file asynchronous-I/O mode. This is modeled resource state, not a requirement-success Boolean or a guessed creator-call list.

types.name: ThreadInfo
types.description: The actual current OS thread: identity is its abstract thread identity; handle is its platform thread handle; phase is starting, running, exit_destructors or exited; tls is the actual current OS TLS key-to-value map; stack is its source stack range. Running TLS destructors is an exit path even though the thread still exists.

types.name: Implementation
types.description: A source trait implementation: type is Self TypeInfo; trait is its source trait name; methods maps source names to method records (name, defining_trait, specialized, invocations); constants maps associated constant names to their source values.

operators.name: get_arg
operators.description: The indexed source argument, receiver first; structured source values and pointer metadata are preserved.

operators.name: get_result
operators.description: The source result. All values also carry invocation metadata via field call, even a unit result. A trait-item contract has an abstract call context whose invocations range over all relevant implementations/member calls; it does not invent a result for an unnamed method.

operators.name: get_field
operators.description: Project a real Rust source field or explicitly defined modeled metadata field. Integer selectors index sequences; string selectors index source-name maps. Pointer/reference wrappers expose their logical source object fields without an extra ABI indirection. A field must have the definition below or be grounded in the supplied Rust source; a suggestive name alone never defines a new property.

operators.name: get_allocation
operators.description: Returns the allocation/provenance object associated with a pointer-like value.

operators.name: memory_range
operators.description: Constructs a half-open byte range [ptr.address, ptr.address + size).

operators.name: memory_between
operators.description: Constructs the half-open byte range between two addresses, independent of their order.

operators.name: offset_does_not_wrap
operators.description: Uses mathematical 128-bit arithmetic to check that ptr plus a signed offset, an unsigned add offset, or an unsigned sub offset does not cross the address-space boundary. direction is signed, add, or sub.

operators.name: mul_fits
operators.description: Uses 128-bit mathematical multiplication and checks that the result fits the target integer type. target is one of isize, usize, i32, u32, i64, or u64; pointer-sized targets use KLEE's current pointer width. Plain operands are non-negative mathematical integers; wrap a signed operand with as_signed.

operators.name: as_signed
operators.description: Interprets a bit-vector value as isize, i32, or i64 and sign-extends it for mathematical arithmetic.

operators.name: get_type_at_func
operators.description: Returns metadata for the indexed type parameter of the target callee.

operators.name: is_power_of_two
operators.description: Returns whether x is a non-zero power of two.

operators.name: is_valid_for
operators.description: Reusable range predicate. The access argument selects precisely one property; it does not imply the other properties. read/write/read_write: the entire half-open range lies in one currently live allocation with that access permission (write requires writable storage); zero-byte ranges are vacuously valid. These modes impose no alignment or initialization. initialized: the range contains initialized Rust values of the optional type_info (otherwise the range element type); each value obeys Rust language validity, including discriminants, references and niches, without requiring padding bytes to be written. bit_valid: the stored bits satisfy only Rust language type validity. invariants: the type-defined safety invariants, beyond language-level bit validity, hold for the values; type_info identifies the type contract. drop/async_drop: precisely the type-defined precondition for the respective destructor, including additional type invariants. utf8/wtf8: the bytes in exactly the range encode that format, without adding allocation/alignment requirements. shared_borrow/read_no_mutation: no conflicting write occurs throughout the returned reference lifetime, except inside UnsafeCell. unique_borrow: accesses during that lifetime must be derived from the returned unique reference. volatile_read_no_race: no unordered overlapping write; volatile_write_no_race: no unordered overlapping other access. exclusive_during_drop: while the destructor runs, all overlapping accesses derive from its supplied self references. no_use_after_drop: no access to the dropped value after destruction. Each temporal mode refers to the current invocation/result lifetime; it is not a call-time capability approximation. Unknown access strings are not defined and must not be invented.

operators.name: c_str_in_allocation
operators.description: Returns whether a non-null pointer has a reachable nul byte before the first uninitialized byte and before the end of the same live KLEE allocation. Symbolic pointers are resolved as a disjunction over live objects.

operators.name: has_nul_terminator
operators.description: Returns whether ptr has a reachable initialized nul terminator in a live KLEE allocation, including for symbolic pointer values.

operators.name: is_convertible_to_ref
operators.description: Atomic predicate for Rust raw-pointer-to-reference convertibility.

constants.name: USIZE_BITS
constants.description: Number of bits in Rust usize.

source_value_semantics: Pointer plus/minus a mathematical byte integer produces a logical derived Pointer, preserving provenance and the source snapshot, with the corresponding mathematical address and offset. This does not silently assert in-bounds or address-space fit. Pointer subtraction produces mathematical byte distance. Recorded values preserve their observation state through field projection, pointer arithmetic and memory_range; is_valid_for on such a range evaluates the referenced bytes in that observation state. On ordinary current-call values it uses the current evaluation state. Sequence iteration binds elements; map iteration binds source-name keys, requiring get_field(map,key) to retrieve mapped records. No hypothetical observation may be inferred from an actual history-only collection. Trait CallContext.invocations explicitly includes hypothetical invocations for each permitted implementation/input. Event invocation identifies its causal source invocation; parent_invocation identifies its causal caller. CallContext identity is the current invocation identity; these identities scope call-caused events. Event unsafe_context records the Rust unsafe/safe source-code context, not semantic correctness. TypeInfo valid_values includes safety invariants, while valid_bit_patterns includes only language validity. Returned references/futures expose Value.lifetime. For a trait method, enclosing type parameter indexes precede method parameters; Self is accessed through the logical receiver type rather than inserted into those indexes. CallContext.types maps actual in-scope source type names/aliases to TypeInfo. CallContext.caller is the logical calling ownership principal; thread_info is ThreadInfo; stack is the dynamic enclosing Invocation sequence; phase is runtime_initialization, running, runtime_cleanup or thread_exit, derived from the actual runtime lifecycle. Invocation.leaf_calls is the transitive collection of actual external primitive calls, excluding intermediate pure Rust helpers; their names identify the actual target API rather than an invented function-name allowlist. State.resources is the modeled OS resource set, State.environment is the actual process environment map, and Event.resource is the resource affected by that access (including environment accesses on targets without a global environ). Resource state on recorded values is the state at that observation. Scalar source values transparently denote their scalar contents; ordering comparisons on pointers compare numerical addresses. Object handles/ObjectId compare stable identity; projecting identity on an object handle yields that same stable identity. These views do not assert type validity or any unmentioned safety requirement. Event.causal_ancestors is the transitive set of invocation identities that caused the event, excluding the directly owning Event.invocation. It includes nested helper calls under the outer source call, but excludes unrelated interrupt/signal handlers. Event.state is the source State snapshot at event.time. CallContext.time and state are the currently evaluated trace position and State (they advance inside temporal formulas); State.active_invocations is the set of active invocation identities at that state. Ordinary CallContext.stack remains its enclosing frames, not a guarantee that its own frame is included. ObjectId and InvocationId are typed source handles: get_field resolves the actual object/invocation record by that identity in its observation state, preserving that state through further projections. This permits Event.object.type and Event.invocation.stack when the handle is well formed; it never grants fields on arbitrary integers or establishes safety merely from a name. A reference type may contain other borrowed references in its pointee; traversal of only ownership descendants does not enumerate those nested borrows. Unnamed Rust tuple/enum-payload fields may be selected by their integer position or its decimal source field-name string (0 or "0"); collection sequence indexing still uses integer positions. Invocation fields have the same definitions as CallContext fields. Source implementation methods maps contain explicit source impl entries; inherited trait default bodies are not inserted as explicit overrides.
